skill.name: effect-lookup
skill.description: Quick lookup for Effect TypeScript library APIs, patterns, and source code. Use when you need to find Effect functions, understand Effect patterns, or look up implementation details.
skill.body:
# Effect Library Lookup

Quick reference for finding and understanding Effect TypeScript library APIs from the local git subtree at `docs/effect/`.

## When to Use This Skill

Use this skill when:

- Looking up Effect function signatures or implementations
- Finding examples of Effect patterns (Effect.gen, Layer, Context, etc.)
- Understanding how Effect modules work internally
- Checking API availability or deprecation status
- Learning Effect idioms from source code

## How to Look Up Effect APIs

### 1. Use the Effect Docs MCP Server (Fastest)

The `effect-docs` MCP server provides indexed documentation:

```
mcp__effect-docs__effect_docs_search: Search for Effect concepts
mcp__effect-docs__get_effect_doc: Get specific documentation by ID
```

### 2. Search the Git Subtree Source

For implementation details, search the local source at `docs/effect/`:

```bash
# Find a specific function
grep -r "export const myFunction" docs/effect/packages/effect/src/

# Find usage patterns
grep -rn "Effect.gen" docs/effect/packages/effect/src/

# Find type definitions
grep -rn "interface MyType" docs/effect/packages/effect/src/
```

### 3. Read Source Files Directly

Core modules are at: `docs/effect/packages/effect/src/<Module>.ts`

Example: To understand `Effect.map`, read `docs/effect/packages/effect/src/Effect.ts`

## Quick Reference

| Task              | Reference                |
| ----------------- | ------------------------ |
| Module categories | `references/modules.md`  |
| Common patterns   | `references/patterns.md` |

## Package Structure

```text
docs/effect/
├── packages/
│   ├── effect/               # Core Effect library
│   │   └── src/              # Source files (Effect.ts, Layer.ts, etc.)
│   ├── platform/             # Cross-platform utilities (HTTP, FileSystem)
│   ├── platform-node/        # Node.js platform implementation
│   ├── platform-browser/     # Browser platform implementation
│   ├── cli/                  # CLI building utilities
│   ├── sql/                  # SQL database utilities
│   ├── sql-pg/               # PostgreSQL implementation
│   ├── sql-kysely/           # Kysely integration
│   ├── rpc/                  # Remote procedure calls
│   ├── cluster/              # Distributed computing
│   ├── opentelemetry/        # OpenTelemetry integration
│   ├── experimental/         # Experimental features
│   └── ai/                   # AI integrations (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)
```

## Core Modules Quick Lookup

### Effect System

| Module  | File         | Purpose                          |
| ------- | ------------ | -------------------------------- |
| Effect  | `Effect.ts`  | Core effect type and combinators |
| Layer   | `Layer.ts`   | Dependency injection layers      |
| Context | `Context.ts` | Type-safe service context        |
| Scope   | `Scope.ts`   | Resource management              |
| Runtime | `Runtime.ts` | Effect execution                 |

### Data Types

| Module  | File         | Purpose                |
| ------- | ------------ | ---------------------- |
| Option  | `Option.ts`  | Optional values        |
| Either  | `Either.ts`  | Success/failure values |
| Chunk   | `Chunk.ts`   | Immutable arrays       |
| HashMap | `HashMap.ts` | Immutable hash maps    |
| HashSet | `HashSet.ts` | Immutable hash sets    |
| List    | `List.ts`    | Immutable linked lists |

### Concurrency

| Module    | File           | Purpose              |
| --------- | -------------- | -------------------- |
| Fiber     | `Fiber.ts`     | Lightweight threads  |
| Queue     | `Queue.ts`     | Concurrent queues    |
| Ref       | `Ref.ts`       | Mutable references   |
| Semaphore | `Semaphore.ts` | Concurrency limiting |
| PubSub    | `PubSub.ts`    | Publish/subscribe    |

### Schema & Validation

| Module      | File             | Purpose                    |
| ----------- | ---------------- | -------------------------- |
| Schema      | `Schema.ts`      | Data validation & encoding |
| ParseResult | `ParseResult.ts` | Parsing results            |
| Arbitrary   | `Arbitrary.ts`   | Property-based testing     |

### Streaming

| Module  | File         | Purpose                 |
| ------- | ------------ | ----------------------- |
| Stream  | `Stream.ts`  | Effectful streams       |
| Sink    | `Sink.ts`    | Stream consumers        |
| Channel | `Channel.ts` | Bidirectional streaming |

### Scheduling & Time

| Module   | File          | Purpose                |
| -------- | ------------- | ---------------------- |
| Schedule | `Schedule.ts` | Retry/repeat schedules |
| Duration | `Duration.ts` | Time durations         |
| DateTime | `DateTime.ts` | Date/time handling     |
| Clock    | `Clock.ts`    | Time service           |
| Cron     | `Cron.ts`     | Cron expressions       |

### Configuration

| Module         | File                | Purpose                 |
| -------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Config         | `Config.ts`         | Type-safe configuration |
| ConfigProvider | `ConfigProvider.ts` | Configuration sources   |

## Common Lookup Patterns

### Find Function Signature

```bash
# In Effect.ts, functions are well-documented with JSDoc
grep -A 20 "export const map" docs/effect/packages/effect/src/Effect.ts
```

### Find Type Definition

```bash
# Look for interface or type alias
grep -n "interface Effect<" docs/effect/packages/effect/src/Effect.ts
```

### Find Examples in Tests

```bash
# Tests often have practical examples
grep -rn "Effect.gen" docs/effect/packages/effect/test/
```

### Check Platform APIs

```bash
# HTTP client/server
ls docs/effect/packages/platform/src/Http*.ts

# FileSystem
cat docs/effect/packages/platform/src/FileSystem.ts
```

## External References

- [Effect Website](https://effect.website/) - Official documentation
- [Effect API Reference](https://effect-ts.github.io/effect/) - Full API docs
- [Effect Discord](https://discord.gg/hdt7t7jpvn) - Community support

## Tips for Effective Lookups

1. **Start with MCP search** - Use `effect_docs_search` for conceptual questions
1. **Read JSDoc comments** - Effect source has excellent inline documentation
1. **Check tests for examples** - Test files show real usage patterns
1. **Use module tables above** - Quickly navigate to the right source file
1. **Platform packages** - HTTP, FileSystem, etc. are in `@effect/platform`

generated_query: I'm implementing retry logic for an HTTP request in Effect TypeScript. I need to use the `Schedule` module to create an exponential backoff schedule with a max of 3 retries and a base delay of 200ms. Can you look up the signature for `Schedule.exponential` and `Schedule.recurs`? Also show me how to combine them with `retry` or `repeat` on an effect, and give a concrete example using `Effect.retry`. Include the actual import paths from the Effect library.

edit_instructions.rationale: Removing the direct mapping to the Schedule module makes it significantly harder to locate the signatures for Schedule.exponential and Schedule.recurs via the lookup tables.

# Effect Schedule & Retry Guide

Covers common retry and repeat schedules using the `Schedule` module. Use this skill when you need to apply retry logic with fixed delays, exponential backoff, or repetition limits.

## Import Paths

All imports from the Effect library use the `effect` package:

```typescript
import { Effect } from "effect/Effect"
import { Schedule } from "effect/Schedule"
import { Duration } from "effect/Duration"
```

## Defining Schedules

### Fixed Delay with `Schedule.spaced`

Creates a schedule that delays a fixed amount between repetitions:

```typescript
const fixedSchedule = Schedule.spaced(Duration.millis(200))
```

### Limited Retries with `Schedule.recurs`

Limits the number of retries. Often used as a final step after a spacing schedule:

```typescript
const limitedSchedule = Schedule.recurs(3)
```

### Combining Schedules

Schedules can be combined using `|>` (pipe) or the `Schedule.andThen` function. The most common pattern is to apply a spacing schedule first, then cap the total retries:

```typescript
const retrySchedule = Schedule.spaced(Duration.millis(200)) |> Schedule.recurs(3)
```

Note: When using `|>`, the first schedule is applied for each retry, and the second limits the total number of repetitions. This gives a fixed 200ms delay between each of the 3 retries.

### Exponential Backoff with `Schedule.exponential`

For exponential backoff, use `Schedule.exponential` directly:

```typescript
const expBase = Duration.millis(200)
const exponentialSchedule = Schedule.exponential(expBase, 2) // doubles each time
```

`Schedule.exponential` takes the base delay and an optional factor (default 2). It does **not** include a retry limit – you must combine it with `Schedule.recurs` separately.

## Applying Schedules with `Effect.retry`

To attach a schedule to an effect, use `Effect.retry`:

```typescript
const failingEffect = Effect.fail("Network error")
const retried = Effect.retry(failingEffect, Schedule.recurs(3))
```

However, `Effect.retry` expects a **single schedule** as its second argument. It does **not** automatically compose schedules passed as a pipeline. To use an exponential schedule with a retry limit, you must wrap the composition inside a single schedule object.

### Standard Pattern: Fixed Delay with Cap

```typescript
import { Effect } from "effect/Effect"
import { Schedule } from "effect/Schedule"
import { Duration } from "effect/Duration"

const program = Effect.retry(
  Effect.sync(() => {
    // HTTP request that may fail
    if (Math.random() < 0.7) throw new Error("Timeout")
    return "Success"
  }),
  Schedule.spaced(Duration.millis(200)) |> Schedule.recurs(3)
)
```

### Exponential Backoff Without Cap (Not Recommended)

```typescript
const expOnly = Effect.retry(httpEffect, Schedule.exponential(Duration.millis(200)))
```

This will retry forever with exponentially increasing delays. The query asks for a max of 3 retries – for that you need to combine exponential with recurs.

## How to Combine Exponential with Recurs

Combining `Schedule.exponential` and `Schedule.recurs` is done by piping one into the other. The result must be a valid `Schedule` object. Here’s the correct composition:

```typescript
const backoffSchedule = Schedule.exponential(Duration.millis(200)) |> Schedule.recurs(3)
```

Then apply it:

```typescript
const effectWithRetry = Effect.retry(
  // your effect
  Effect.fail("Error"),
  backoffSchedule
)
```

**Important**: The order matters. Placing `Schedule.recurs` first would limit retries before exponential delays, giving different behavior.

## Alternative: Using `Effect.repeat`

`Effect.repeat` works identically to `Effect.retry` but operates on success values instead of failures. For retry-on-failure, always use `Effect.retry`.

## Full Example with Import Paths

```typescript
import { Effect } from "effect/Effect"
import { Schedule } from "effect/Schedule"
import { Duration } from "effect/Duration"

const request = Effect.tryPromise(() =>
  fetch("https://api.example.com/data")
)

const schedule = Schedule.exponential(Duration.millis(200)) |> Schedule.recurs(3)

const retried = Effect.retry(request, schedule)

Effect.runPromise(retried)
```

This example uses the correct imports and schedule composition. However, note that `Effect.retry` may fail if the schedule type is not fully compatible – see the table below for schedule compatibility.

## Schedule Compatibility Table

| Schedule Type         | Retry Limit? | Works with `Effect.retry`? |
|-----------------------|--------------|----------------------------|
| `Schedule.spaced`     | No           | Yes                        |
| `Schedule.exponential`| No           | Yes                        |
| `Schedule.recurs`     | Yes (count)  | Yes                        |
| Composed via `\|>`    | Depends      | Often yes, but not always  |

If you encounter type errors when composing schedules, consider using `Schedule.union` or `Schedule.intersection` for stricter guarantees.

## Debugging Schedules

Print schedule decisions:

```typescript
Schedule.whileInput((retryCount) => {
  console.log(`Retry #${retryCount}`)
  return true
})
```

Then pipe into your schedule for logging.
